description: Hundreds of Nigerian women protested at the National Assembly after five bills were rejected: on citizenship, reserved parliamentary seats, affirmative action, and indigeneship - the last of which would have allowed women to become natives of their husbands' states.
energy_note: Five bills, one morning, all rejected.

description: The Senate rejected the Gender and Equal Opportunities Bill on 15 December 2021 for the second time, having first been presented in 2016. Male lawmakers argued the Constitution already upholds women's rights. The bill also sought to protect widows' rights and discourage gender discrimination.
energy_note: Rejected twice, on the grounds that it was unnecessary.

aspect: VAPP exists and is federal in a federal country
description: The Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) Act 2015 is the most comprehensive legislation on violence against women - covering domestic violence, rape, FGM/C and child marriage - but as a federal law it is directly effective only in the Federal Capital Territory. States must domesticate it. Kano has not.
energy_note: A national law that stops at the edge of Abuja.

description: In August 2024 a bill to repeal the VAPP Act advanced to second reading in the Senate, drawing opposition from women's rights groups.
energy_note: Nine years old, and already at second reading for repeal.

aspect: The pattern is what matters, not any single vote
description: Each refusal is individually explicable. Together they describe a legislature that has declined, repeatedly and recently, to alter the position of women in law - which is why the remedies referenced elsewhere in this dataset keep being customary rather than statutory.
energy_note: Not one decision. A consistent answer.
